To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The snow-covered period is an important period for trace-gas exchange between the atmosphere and alpine and subalpine ecosystems.

(1) The flux of carbon dioxide (CO2) and nitrous oxide (N2O) through a Wyoming snow pack is significant and the flux of methane (CH4) is substantial, and (2) These fluxes represent a substantial portion of the annual trace gas budget for these ecosystems.
“We found that the soils under a Wyoming snowpack emit CO2 and take up CH4 and N20 throughout the winter.”

the flux of CO2, CH4, and N2O through the snowpack and the underlying soils.
the flux of trace gases through the snowpack.
the role of the snowpack in the global trace-gas budget.

the fluxes of the three gases through the snowpacks of the alpine and subalpine regions of the world are important to the global budgets of these gases.
snowpacks are not sinks for atmospheric CO _{2}, but rather sources, with the fluxes being controlled by snowpack thickness, temperature, and soil moisture.
the snow cover is a sink for atmospheric CH4 and a source of CO2, N2O and possibly CH4, depending upon snowpack thickness and depth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
snowpacks are not just a barrier to gas fluxes but also act as a conduit for gas fluxes.

the fluxes are large enough to be of global significance, that they occur at a time when they are most needed (the winter), that they are large enough to influence atmospheric chemistry, that they are large compared to the fluxes of trace-gas exchange that have been measured at lower elevations, that they occur in a region where the trace-gas fluxes have been poorly studied, and that they are large in relation to the amount of soil that is covered by snow.

we found that the snow pack is an active environment for microbial respiration and that the fluxes of CO2, CH4, and N2O from this ecosystem are much larger than previously thought.
the snowpack is not a passive layer that stops trace-gas fluxes.
snowpack is a significant source of CO2, a sink of CH4 and a source of N2O in alpine and high-latitude ecosystems.
